no style, please! (Jekyll theme)

An open-source blog theme with about 1 kB of CSS that leaves almost everything at browser defaults.

Source
GitHub: riggraz/no-style-please
Creator
Riccardo Graziosi (riggraz)
Made
2020
Style
Brutalist web design (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Raw, plain, honest
Evidence
Opened the repository’s README screenshot _screenshots/featured-image.png (2678 × 1500 px) with the Read tool on 2026-10-02, and read _sass/no-style-please.scss. Repository created 10 July 2020 (GitHub API). The live demo was not captured.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: MIT. Rights policy

Context

The README describes it as “A (nearly) no-CSS, fast, minimalist Jekyll theme”, “Inspired by elly’s site”, with “1kb of CSS”.

The stylesheet sets color: black; font-family: monospace; font-size: 16px on a white body, a 640 px column, and a dark mode made with filter: invert(1). It does not set link colors.

MIT license. A Hugo port exists: hanwenguo/hugo-theme-nostyleplease (2022).

Observed

  • The light screenshot shows a bold monospace title, “no style, please!”, above a nested bulleted list with disc, circle, and square markers.
  • Links are underlined; unvisited links are bright blue and visited links purple, as in browser defaults.
  • Post dates in ISO form (2020-07-09) sit before each link. No images, rules, boxes, or shadows.
  • The dark screenshot is the same page inverted: white monospace on black, with a yellow footnote link.

Why it belongs

A clear current example of Brutalist web design in the monospace variant that NN/g (2017) describes: “blue links and monochromatic Monospace text”.

Borrow

Use nested lists as navigation and let the default bullet shapes show the hierarchy.

Make a dark mode by inverting the page instead of designing a second palette.
